answer: In an agent trading haven, every seller, whether offering a quill or a piece of onyx, must lock 100 credits for 30 days before receiving one job slot per day. Extra identities gain no exemption: each needs its own bond. An attacker seeking 1,000 daily slots must therefore immobilize 100,000 credits for a month. Creating names is cheap, but scaling their access ties up capital and sacrifices its use elsewhere.
